app.name: SurvivalCheck
app.tagline: Check your household's readiness for emergencies, calmly.
app.subtitle: A calm guide for a prepared household

common.not_applicable: Does not apply to this household
common.evidence_snippet: From an excerpt, to be re-checked
common.coming_soon_body: This section is being prepared and will be available in an upcoming update.

home.title: Welcome
home.intro: SurvivalCheck shows how prepared your household is for a disaster and suggests small next steps. Rough numbers are enough to begin.
home.privacy: Your data stays on this device. No account, no tracking, and the app keeps working without internet.
home.mode_hint: Quick mode gives a first picture. You can complete it later.

steps.profile: Tell us who is in your household
steps.target: Choose a target and the emergencies to plan for
steps.inventory: Fill in the supplies you have
steps.result: See your result and next steps

home.install_body: Install the app so it opens quickly and works without a signal.
home.update_available: A new data version is available.
home.reminder_check_bag: It has been 6 months. Time to re-check your go-bag and expiry dates.
home.reminder_drill: Try a family evacuation drill. Twice a year is recommended.
home.reminder_water: Replace water you filled yourself (every 6 months).
home.reminder_power: Recharge power banks and power stations (every 3 months).
home.partial_note: No stock entered yet, so this number is only a first estimate.
home.next_food: Pick one kind of food you have at home and enter how much.

disclaimer.title: Good to know
disclaimer.short: This app does not replace instructions from local authorities (BNPB, BPBD, BMKG, health workers). For medicines and chemicals, always follow the label and health professionals.
disclaimer.full: SurvivalCheck is a planning aid, not medical, legal, or technical advice. In an emergency, follow BNPB, BPBD, BMKG, officials, and health workers in your area. The amounts shown are general estimates from official guidance. Your household may need different amounts. Doses for medicines, bleach, iodine, and water purification tablets always follow the product label and health professionals' advice.
disclaimer.footer_print: Not a substitute for local authority instructions. Printed {date}.

profile.title: Household profile
profile.intro: Who do you look after? These numbers are used to work out water, food, and medicine needs.
profile.pregnancy_hint: Energy needs increase. For water, official guidance only says to drink more, without a fixed amount.
profile.meds_intro: Add medicines a family member takes regularly. Only doses and remaining stock are needed, not the full name.
profile.meds_stock_days: Current stock lasts how many days
profile.meds_empty: No regular medicines yet. Skip if there are none.
profile.meds_note: Ask your doctor or pharmacist how to build up a stock of regular medicines. Do not change doses on your own.
profile.pets_food_per_day: Food per day (what you usually give)
profile.pets_hint: Pets are counted as an extra and do not decide your tier.
profile.baby_intro: Fill in your baby's daily use. There is no standard amount, so we use your own numbers.
profile.baby_formula_unit: scoops or bottles, as on the pack
profile.baby_breastfed_hint: Breastfeeding is still encouraged. Keep some formula as a backup if needed.
profile.special_aids: Uses aids (wheelchair, cane, hearing aid, glasses)
profile.special_electric_medical: Uses medical equipment that needs electricity
profile.special_electric_hint: Examples are a CPAP, oxygen concentrator, nebulizer, or medicine fridge. We will help work out the power needed in the Power step.
profile.altitude: Live above 1,000 m above sea level
profile.altitude_hint: Water needs to be boiled longer at altitude (3 minutes).
profile.province_hint: We use BNPB risk data (IRBI 2024) to suggest emergencies to plan for. You can still change them.
profile.province_note_jatim: Note: IRBI data for East Java is identical to DI Yogyakarta, so please double-check the suggestion.

validation.no_people: Enter at least one person so the calculation can start.
validation.too_many: That is a very large number. Please check it.
validation.count_exceeds_adults: More pregnant or breastfeeding people than adults. Please check.
validation.doses_range: Doses per day must be between 1 and 12.

profile.summary_saved: Profile saved. On to your target.

target.title: Survival target
target.intro: How many days do you want to be ready to last at home?
target.bnpb_min: BNPB minimum: 3 days (72 hours). Many countries now recommend 7 days or more, which is why 7 days is our starting choice.
target.below_min: A target below 3 days is under the BNPB minimum. You may still use it.
target.scenario_intro: Choose one or more. Shared items are not counted twice, and the largest requirement is used.
target.scenario_suggested_hint: Based on BNPB risk data. Untick anything that does not fit.
target.scenario_none: No specific emergency chosen? The core pack (water, food, medicine, sanitation, lighting, communication, documents, go-bag) is still counted.
target.effective_duration_why: Because of {scenario}, the target is raised from {from} to {to} days.
target.water_raised: Drinking water is raised to {n} L per person per day.
target.medicine_raised: Regular medicine stock is raised to {n} days.

validation.days_required: Enter a number of days between 1 and 365.
validation.days_large: A target over 90 days is rarely realistic. Continue anyway?

target.water_careful: Cautious figure: 4 L comes from hot-weather guidance (Latvia), not drought-specific. Treat it as a safe margin, not an exact number.
target.lv_bnpb_hint: At least 72 hours, in line with the BNPB go-bag.
target.lv_rec_hint: Beyond the BNPB standard and common in official guides.
target.lv_tough_hint: Needs a way to cook, purify water, and backup power.
target.assume: Assuming a power cut and no running water, {n} people need roughly:
target.change_anytime: You can change this any time.

scenarios.drought_desc: Drinking water rises to 4 L per person per day
scenarios.pandemic_desc: At least 14 days of stock, 30 days of regular medicine
scenarios.note_international: There is no dedicated guidance for residents of Indonesia yet. This content is compiled from official guidance of other countries and international bodies. If Indonesian authorities issue instructions, follow those.

categories.power_desc: Power banks, power stations, solar panels

inventory.title: Supplies
inventory.intro: Enter what you have now. Rough numbers are fine. You can come back any time.
inventory.quick_banner: Quick mode: core questions only. The interim result may be less accurate.
inventory.empty_state_body: Start with one category, such as water. Every entry is saved right away.
inventory.water_note: We use 3 L per person per day for drinking and cooking. Hygiene water of 2 L per person per day is a suggestion and does not hold back your tier.

food.title: Food by type
food.intro: Enter the amount of each type of food you usually keep. The app works out total calories.
food.other_kcal: Other food: enter calories from the label
food.ready_to_eat_tip: Keep part of your stock edible without cooking, since power or gas may be cut.

gobag.title: 72-hour go-bag (BNPB standard)
gobag.intro: Tick what is already in the bag. This list follows the 28 items from BNPB.
gobag.skip_infant: No infant or toddler: baby items are not counted.
gobag.skip_elder: No older adult: elder medicine item is not counted.
gobag.excluded_note: Items that do not apply are left out of the calculation.
gobag.bag_tip: Keep the bag somewhere easy to reach, and make sure everyone at home knows where it is.

validation.very_large: That number is very large. Is it right?
validation.expiry_past: This date has passed. Expired items are not counted as stock.

inventory.fuel_days_label: Enough for how many days of cooking
inventory.fuel_suggest: Suggested amount, not a requirement: about {per} canisters per person per week. For {n} people over {days} days: about {cans} canisters.

power.title: Power
power.intro: Work out how much electricity you need during an outage and compare it with what you have. Every number can be changed to match your device label.
power.devices_intro: Pick the devices that must keep running. Typical watts are pre-filled and can be changed.
power.watts_hint: Check the label on the device. Typical numbers are only estimates.
power.surge_note: Motor-driven devices (pump, fridge) draw more power when starting.
power.outage_days: How many days of outage do you want to cover?
power.wh_explain: Wh (watt-hour) is a unit of energy: power multiplied by hours of use.
power.recommend_why: Includes inverter efficiency, a capacity reserve, and the largest device's power draw.
power.recommend_none: Pick devices first to see a suggestion.

owned.power_bank_note: The mAh on the label is measured at battery voltage, not 5 V, so the conversion is only an estimate.
owned.generator_fuel: Fuel available for how many hours

power.coverage: Power is enough for about {n} days
power.coverage_short: About {n} Wh short of your target.
power.medical_gating: Because medical equipment needs electricity, power now counts toward how many days you can manage.
power.medical_registry: If someone at home depends on medical equipment, ask PLN and your nearest health facility about priority customer registration. Procedures and services can differ by area.
power.solar_self_sufficient: This panel can cover the daily needs of the devices you chose.
power.solar_not_enough: This panel covers only part of the daily need. The rest comes from stored battery.
power.solar_cloudy: Panel output drops when it is cloudy or raining.

warn.co_body: Never run a generator, stove, or charcoal grill indoors, in a garage, or near windows and vents. CO gas has no smell and can be life-threatening. Keep them outdoors, away from buildings.
warn.co_symptoms: If you feel dizzy, sick, or short of breath, get to fresh air immediately and seek medical help.
warn.house_wiring_title: Do not connect a generator to your home wiring yourself
warn.house_wiring_body: Connecting a generator to home wiring without a technician and safety equipment can send power back into the grid and endanger workers. Use extension cords straight to devices, or ask a licensed technician.
warn.dry_body: Keep power stations and batteries dry, cool, and away from water. Follow the manufacturer's instructions.

power.empty_state_body: Start with your phone and a light. Add others if needed. You may also skip this step.

validation.hours_range: Hours of use must be between 0 and 24.

family_eval.title: Family evaluation
family_eval.intro: Eighteen questions from BNPB to see how ready your family is. Answer based on how things are today; the result is used to pick your next step.
family_eval.context_quake_flood: This question is mainly about earthquakes or floods. Please still answer it so your score matches the BNPB standard.

q.2: The go-bag is checked at least every 6 months
q.3: Everyone knows where the go-bag is
q.4: Important documents are kept in waterproof plastic
q.5: There is a flashlight in the bedroom
q.6: There is a reserve of clean water in the rainy season
q.7: Personal medicine is always in the bag
q.8: An evacuation route has been agreed
q.9: There is a meeting point outside the home
q.10: Everyone knows Drop, Cover, Hold On during an earthquake
q.11: The family has done an earthquake drill
q.12: It is clear who takes the go-bag
q.13: It is clear who helps children and older adults
q.14: The family has practiced calming breathing
q.15: Children know who to follow in an emergency
q.16: The family knows not to re-enter the house during aftershocks
q.17: The family knows early flood signs and when to evacuate
q.18: Emergency numbers are printed and easy to see

family_eval.empty_state: Not answered yet. Start with the first question.

0.name: Not ready yet
0.summary: You are at the start. One small step is enough to reach the next tier.

1.name: Vulnerable
1.summary: You have supplies for 1 to 2 days. A few key things still need filling in.

2.name: Basic ready 72 hours (BNPB standard)
2.summary: You meet the BNPB basic standard for 3 days.

3.name: Ready for 1 week
3.summary: You go beyond the BNPB standard and are ready for about 7 days.

4.name: Resilient for 2 weeks
4.summary: Ready for about 14 days, with a way to cook and purify water.

5.name: Self-reliant 30 days or more
5.summary: Ready for 30 days or more, with alternative power and first-aid skills.

bag.title: Go-bag (BNPB)
bag.rule: Above 80% is ready, 50 to 80% needs more, below 50% is not ready. Exactly 80% counts as needs more.

family.title: Family evaluation (BNPB)
family.rule: Scores 0 to 12 are vulnerable, 13 to 24 fairly prepared, 25 to 36 ready.

result.title: Readiness result
result.calm_intro: This result shows the next steps for your household.
result.empty_body: Fill in your profile and some supplies first, then your result will appear here.
result.partial_banner: Interim result. Some data is missing, so numbers may be lower than reality.
result.bottleneck_ok: All key resources cover your target.
result.survive_note: Worked out from whichever runs out first among drinking water, calories, regular medicine, baby food, and power for medical equipment (if any).
result.score_note: The score is an extra view. Your tier is decided by key items, not by the score.
result.bnpb_family_missing: Family evaluation not filled in yet.
result.next_gate_family: Family evaluation needs a score of at least {n} out of 36.
result.next_gate_bag: The go-bag needs to be more than 80% filled.
result.next_gate_days: All critical stock needs to cover {n} days.
result.next_top: You are at the highest tier. Keep it up by checking your stock regularly.
result.next_hint: Take one small step first. Finish one item below, then check again.
result.shortfall_empty: Nothing is missing for this target.
result.no_price_note: This app does not show prices. Store chain names are only general examples, not brand or store recommendations.
result.recalc: The result is recalculated automatically when data changes.
result.next_group_fuel: Cooking fuel for {days} days. Any one is enough: {items}

shopping.title: Shopping list
shopping.intro: Grouped by type of store so you can shop in one trip. Tick what you have bought.
shopping.empty_body: Nothing is missing for this target, or your data is not filled in yet.
shopping.copy_failed: Could not copy automatically. Use print or download instead.
shopping.print_tip: Choose Save as PDF in the print dialog to save without paper.
shopping.check_label_note: For bleach, iodine, and tablets: check the strength and instructions on the label.
shopping.rx_note: Prescription medicine: ask your doctor, health facility, or pharmacist. Do not buy prescription-only medicine without a prescription.

stores.examples_label: General examples (examples only, not a recommendation)

info.title: More
info.offline_note: Every page here works without internet.

emergency.title: Emergency numbers
emergency.n112: 112: unified emergency service (fire, accidents, disasters, health, security)
emergency.n112_caveat: 112 availability depends on your area. If it does not connect, use the numbers below.
emergency.n119_spgdt: 119: Ministry of Health medical emergency (SPGDT), also via SATUSEHAT Mobile
emergency.verify_note: Some numbers come from 2019 to 2020 guides. Also save the numbers of your local BPBD and health center.

channels.title: Official information channels
channels.online_only: These channels need internet. Save numbers and guides from this page before you need them.

guides.title: Guides by emergency type
guides.not_substitute: These short guides do not replace instructions from officials on site.
guides.tsunami_lead: If you feel a strong or long earthquake near the coast, move to high ground right away. Do not wait for a siren or official warning.
guides.tsunami_note: The 20-20-20 rule is only one rule of thumb in some regions and does not apply everywhere. Do not use it as a reason to wait.
guides.conflict_lead: There is no preparedness guidance on conflict aimed at residents of Indonesia yet. This content draws on official guidance from other countries (for example Sweden, Norway, Estonia) and is an international reference only.
guides.nuclear_lead: There is no dedicated guidance for residents of Indonesia yet. This content draws on international references (CDC, UK, Finland, Poland) and is a general overview only. Follow the competent authorities.
guides.ki_body: Potassium iodide tablets are not on the shopping list and should not be taken on your own. Take them only if the competent authorities instruct you to, and follow the dose they give.
guides.nuclear_shelter: Shelter indoors for at least 24 hours or until told otherwise.

before: Fasten furniture to walls (nails or straps); keep heavy items on low shelves.
Pick a safe spot inside the home, plus a main and a backup meeting point outside.
Keep shoes and a flashlight next to your bed.
Prepare a fire extinguisher, whistle and go-bag.
Keep a helmet, or a pillow, ready to protect your head.
during: Drop, Cover, Hold On: get down, take cover and hold on. Do not run while the ground is shaking.
Protect your head with a helmet or a pillow.
When the shaking stops, go to your meeting point.
after: If you see signs of liquefaction, landslide, fire or gas, evacuate sideways, away from the spot.
Put on shoes and take the flashlight you prepared.
Meet at the main meeting point; if you cannot, use the backup one.
At the coast: a strong or long quake means follow the tsunami guide.

before: Learn the evacuation routes and signs and the nearest high ground from home, school and work.
Prepare a go-bag, radio and flashlight.
Practise evacuating on foot with your family.
during: A strong or long earthquake near the coast is the early warning: go to high ground right away. Do not wait for a siren or an official warning.
Move away from the beach and riverbanks.
Evacuate on foot and avoid bridges; leave your vehicle if traffic is stuck.
If you do not know where safe ground is, run as far from the coast as you can and climb higher.
Alert levels AWAS and SIAGA mean evacuate. WASPADA means stay away from the beach and riverbanks.
after: A tsunami can arrive up to 5 times. Do not go back until the authorities say it is safe.
Follow information from national TV, local radio, sirens or kentongan drums.
Keep following the evacuation routes and signs until you reach safe ground.
tsunami.source: BMKG (2021 press release, Earthquake and Tsunami Pocket Book 2020); BNPB

before: Prepare to be self-reliant for at least 3 days.
Keep important documents in waterproof plastic.
Have buckets or containers filled with clean water.
Have a stick and protective shoes ready.
during: Switch off the main power and remove the LPG regulator.
Evacuate before the water reaches knee height; a 30 cm current is already dangerous.
Use a stick to test your footing.
Landslide: move away when you hear a rumble or siren, and watch for further slides.
after: When cleaning, wear gloves and boots and use disinfectant.
Throw away food that was soaked by floodwater.
Drinking water: boil it, or treat it with alum, PAC, tablets or iodine.
Wash hands with soap; protective shoes help prevent leptospirosis.
flood_landslide.source: BNPB 2026 and 2019; Ministry of Health (clean water and infectious disease during floods)

before: Prepare masks and protective goggles.
Prepare ready-to-eat food, a flashlight and batteries, enough cash and special medicines.
Know the hazard radius zones (KRB) and follow MAGMA Indonesia.
during: Respect the hazard radius that has been set.
Wear a mask (or a wet cloth) and protective goggles. Do not wear contact lenses.
Wear long sleeves, long trousers and a hat.
after: Clear ash from the roof.
Watch for lahars when it rains.
Outdoors, keep wearing a mask and protective goggles.
eruption.source: BNPB 2019/2020; Ministry of Energy and Mineral Resources (ESDM) and PVMBG

before: Have an N95 mask for each family member.
Follow air quality readings. BNPB PM10 categories: Good 0-50, Moderate 50-150, Unhealthy 150-250, Very unhealthy 250-350, Hazardous above 350.
Know who is vulnerable: young children, pregnant women, older people, and people with asthma, lung or heart conditions.
during: Stay indoors and close off ways for smoke to get in.
Use air conditioning or air filtration if you have it.
If you must go out, wear an N95 snugly with no gaps.
Vulnerable people should not go outside.
Drink enough water and eat well.
after: Go to a clinic or hospital if you have shortness of breath, a persistent cough, chest pain or severe eye irritation.
Most acute respiratory infections can be treated at home with rest and enough fluids.
Keep checking air quality before going outdoors.
haze.source: BNPB 2019/2020; Ministry of Health (August and October 2026)

before: Install a water tank in your yard to collect rainwater.
BMKG: the 2026 dry season is drier than normal and lasts 3 to 7 months depending on the region.
This app uses 4 L per person per day for this scenario as an assumption (a Latvian reference), not an official Indonesian figure.
during: Save water and set a schedule for using it.
Ask the authorities (local government) for clean water assistance.
after: Keep saving water until the dry season is over.
Collect rainwater in your tank once the rainy season arrives.
drought.source: BNPB 2019/2020; BMKG (June 2026). No official household water figure exists from Indonesian sources

before: Follow BMKG early warnings: rainfall, tropical cyclones, high waves and tidal flooding. BMKG Contact Center: 196.
Make sure your communication device, flashlight and radio are ready.
during: Bring things indoors, lock doors and windows, and switch off the power.
During lightning: crouch down, sit and hug your knees. Do not lie flat.
Stay away from large trees and billboards.
Tidal surge: keep a communication device ready and stay away from the coast.
extreme_weather.source: BNPB 2012 and 2019; BMKG (early warnings, Contact Center 196)

before: Make sure a power bank, a radio and a flashlight with batteries are in your go-bag. Keep one flashlight in the bedroom.
Keep cash and a stove that does not need electricity (Swedish, German and Swiss references).
If you use electric medical equipment, talk to your doctor and equipment provider about a backup plan.
Fill in the Electric power module in this app to estimate how long your power lasts.
during: Gather the family. Use a flashlight, not candles.
Check official information by radio or phone; do not share unconfirmed information.
Do not use a generator, stove or charcoal inside the home, a garage or a semi-enclosed space. Carbon monoxide risk.
Keep the fridge and freezer doors closed.
after: A fridge keeps food safe for about 4 hours; a full freezer about 48 hours. Throw away perishable food after 4 hours without power.
Medicines that must stay cold: ask your doctor or pharmacist before using them after an outage.
power_outage.source: BNPB 2026; CDC and FDA (food and medicine safety); Swedish, German, Swiss and Danish guidance (cash, stove, CO)

before: Keep at least 14 days of water and food, and 30 days of routine medicines.
Have masks, hand sanitizer and a thermometer.
Keep routine immunisations up to date.
during: Wash hands with soap and use hand sanitizer.
Keep at least 1 m apart and wear a mask in public places.
Cover coughs and sneezes properly.
If you have symptoms: isolate yourself and use telemedicine.
Disinfect frequently touched surfaces.
after: In evacuation centres: wear a mask, keep hands clean and report symptoms right away.
Continue routine and catch-up immunisations (measles and pertussis risk).
pandemic.source: BNPB 2020; Ministry of Health 2025; CDC (2-week stock); Germany and Switzerland (FFP2 masks, thermometer)

before: International reference; there is no guidance for Indonesian residents yet. If Indonesian authorities issue instructions, follow them.
Keep food and water for at least 7 days (Swedish, Norwegian and Estonian references).
Keep cash for about 1 week.
Have a radio with batteries or a hand crank.
during: Avoid protest crowds and report riots or violence to the Police (BNPB 2012).
"Two walls" principle (Latvia, Poland): stay where two walls separate you from the outside, away from windows.
Beware of disinformation; check news through radio and official sources.
after: Follow the authorities' instructions before returning home or travelling.
Report suspicious people or plans to the authorities.
conflict.source: Sweden, Norway, Estonia, Latvia and Poland (international references). Indonesia: BNPB 2012 for civil unrest

before: International reference; there is no guidance for Indonesian residents yet. Follow the authorities (BAPETEN, BNPB, local government).
Keep plastic sheeting and tape to seal windows and vents.
Keep a battery radio to follow instructions.
You do not need to stock potassium iodide (KI) tablets. Take them only if the authorities instruct you to.
during: Get inside and stay inside for at least 24 hours, or until told otherwise.
Switch off air conditioning, fans and ventilation; close windows and doors.
Seal gaps with plastic and tape.
Bring pets inside. Do not go out to pick up family.
after: Remove outer clothing; this can remove up to 90% of radioactive material. Then shower.
Take KI only if the authorities tell you to, at the dose they give.
Keep following the radio and the authorities before going out.
nuclear.source: International references: CDC, UK, Finland, Poland, Estonia, Latvia. Indonesia: BAPETEN 2017 (excerpt only, not verified)

water.title: Making water safe
water.label_rule: Strengths of bleach, iodine, and tablets differ by product. Follow the label. If in doubt, boil the water.
water.boil_body: Bring to a rolling boil for 1 minute. Above 1,000 m above sea level, boil for 3 minutes.
water.bleach_body: Only for 5 to 9% bleach without scent or additives. Check the strength on the label first. Add 2 drops per liter, 4 drops if the water is cloudy. Stir and wait 30 minutes. The water should have a faint chlorine smell. If the strength is different or you are unsure, boil instead.
water.iodine_body: Check the strength on the label. 2% strength: 5 drops per liter, 10 drops if the water is cloudy. 7% strength: 2 drops per liter. Stir and let it stand at least 30 minutes before drinking. Do not use if you are allergic to iodine, pregnant, or have a thyroid condition. If unsure, boil instead.
water.tablet_body: Follow the pack instructions for the number of tablets and waiting time.
water.settle_body: Alum about half a teaspoon per 20 liters, or 1 sachet of PAC per 20 liters, then strain and disinfect (boil or bleach).
water.store_tip: Store treated water in a clean, covered container.

family_plan.title: Contact card and family plan
family_plan.intro: Fill it in, print it, put it where it is easy to see, and keep a copy in the go-bag.
family_plan.helper: Who helps children and older adults

sources.title: Sources and references
sources.intro: Main references are BNPB, BMKG, PVMBG, and the Ministry of Health, complemented by official guidance from several countries and international bodies.
sources.evidence_snippet: From an excerpt, to be re-checked
sources.bnpb_citation: BNPB (2026). 72-hour go-bag checklist and family evaluation.

about.title: About the app
about.body: SurvivalCheck helps households in Indonesia plan for emergencies. Main references are BNPB, BMKG, PVMBG, and the Ministry of Health, complemented by official guidance from several countries.
about.no_prices: This app shows no prices and does not recommend brands.

settings.title: Settings
settings.reminders_hint: Reminders only appear when you open the app. No notifications come from a server.
settings.export_hint: Keep this file to move phones or as a backup.
settings.export_done: Backup file is ready to download.
settings.import_hint: Existing data on this device will be replaced.
settings.import_confirm_body: Data on this device will be replaced and cannot be restored. Export first if you want to keep the current data.
settings.import_error_format: This file is not recognized as a SurvivalCheck backup.
settings.import_error_version: This file comes from an unsupported app version.
settings.import_error_read: The file could not be read. Try another file.
settings.delete_hint: Removes your profile, supplies, and settings from this device.
settings.delete_confirm_body: All data on this device will be deleted and cannot be restored. Export first if you want to keep it.
settings.data_update_offline: You are offline. Updates are checked when you are online.
settings.privacy_body: All data stays on this device only. No account, server, or tracking.
settings.storage_unavailable: Browser storage is unavailable, possibly because of private mode. Your data will not be kept after the page is closed.

warnings.label: Attention
warnings.water_3l: BNPB states a minimum of 2 liters of drinking water per person per day. SurvivalCheck uses 3 liters (drinking and cooking) because most official guidance from other countries and the WHO falls around 2.5 to 3 liters, our climate is tropical, and water is also used to prepare food or baby formula. The BNPB 2-liter figure is still shown as the minimum.
warnings.water_drought: During drought, drinking water is raised to 4 liters per person per day.
warnings.dose_label: Doses of medicines, bleach, iodine, and water purification tablets always follow the label and health professionals' advice. If unsure, boil the water or ask a health professional.
warnings.ki_authority: Potassium iodide tablets are taken only on the instruction of the competent authorities. Do not take them on your own.
warnings.tsunami_no_siren: If an earthquake feels strong or long near the coast, move to high ground right away. Do not wait for a siren.
warnings.international_only: International reference. There is no dedicated guidance for residents of Indonesia yet.
warnings.n112_area: Availability of 112 depends on your area.
warnings.candles: Candles are a last-resort backup because of fire risk. Prefer flashlights or headlamps. Never leave a candle burning, and keep it away from curtains and flammable materials.
warnings.flashlight_not_candle: Flashlights, not candles, for main lighting.
warnings.co_genset: Never run a generator, stove, or charcoal grill indoors. CO gas has no smell and can be deadly.
warnings.not_substitute: Not a substitute for local authority instructions.
warnings.pregnancy_water: Pregnant and breastfeeding women are advised to drink more. Official guidance gives no fixed amount.
warnings.medicine_consult: Ask your doctor or pharmacist how to build up a stock of regular medicines.
